JN-001.title: A stranger scans their domain and leaves with a finished page
JN-001.persona: founder who has never heard of ReachKit, arriving from a link or a search

steps.step: Types their domain into the one field on the landing page, or opens a shared report link — and a scan starts, unless a report for that domain already exists

Waits through a scan that names each stage and returns a readable report inside a minute — or, when the scan stops early, gets back an incomplete report that says what is missing and offers them one re-scan there and then, without waiting out the week a finished report waits; or, when the measurement fails, is told in writing what happened and offered a retry; or, when a limit is met, is told in writing which limit it was and, where there is one to give, when they may scan again
Reads the verdict at the top: one score, its band in words, its three drivers, and a dash with a written line wherever something could not be measured
Reads what AI tells buyers — on how many of their market's biggest searches an AI answer appears, which brands it names instead of them, and the search and volume behind each question

Reads their Google presence — their share of those same searches beside each rival, the biggest searches they are absent from, and the standing line saying every figure here was measured on US Google in English and that more countries are coming

Corrects the category when the report has read their business as the wrong kind of market, and returns to the verdict, the AI answers and the Google presence to read them again against the corrected market
Reads the three problems, copies the free robots fix, and reads the complete method in the DIY sections

Reads what the first page would be — its title, what it targets, who it takes ground from, and how many more were found behind it — and gives their email address as the trade, told before they type what else that address will receive
Receives the finished page in their inbox, and at most three follow-ups afterwards, stopping the moment they subscribe or opt out
Chooses Start ReachKit where the price is offered — their own report, or a price surface with no report behind it — and pays €49, having created no account
Opens the sign-in email that the payment produced and lands on setup
If they stop partway, is asked to come back and finish setup, and picks up where they left off
Settles the site address — confirms or corrects the domain their report measured, or types it in when the purchase had no report behind it

Or, where setup will not accept the address they give, reads one written line saying so that names a way to reach a person and says they may cancel without finishing, and finds every answer they have already given still there when they come back
Reads the market we inferred and confirms or corrects it — or states it in their own words, where nothing was measured for the domain their account will use
Confirms who they compete with — the suggestions we found, plus any rival they know and we don't, up to five
Chooses whether pages go out on their own and where they publish, then submits the three decisions once
Watches the deep pass run and arrives inside the app — and, where it found less than a month of pages to write, is told that on arrival rather than weeks later

JN-003.title: The daily page — from tomorrow's plan to a page live on my domain

rests-on.claim: The customer's timezone is captured once and stored as one preference, so 'the evening before', the veto window and 'the next morning' are the customer's own local times throughout this journey — the single stored preference REQ-073 criterion 1 captures with a stated default ('the time zone is the one their browser reported at first sign-in, which they may change here at any time afterwards').

JN-003.persona: A paying solo founder, three weeks into the subscription, who opens ReachKit for five minutes most evenings and expects a page to go out whether or not they do.

steps.step: Opens the app after the evening's notice and looks at the calendar to see what is planned, what is live, and whether anything is waiting on them
Selects tomorrow's page and reads why it exists — the search it targets, who answers that search today, and what would count as it having worked
Opens the full draft and reads it end to end, checking what it is grounded in, that it sounds like their business, and that it makes no claim they forbid

Fixes a sentence they disagree with, watching the page re-render as they type, closes the tab without saving anything explicitly, and where the edit trips their do-not-claim list is told which entry it matched and edits it again
Approves it, vetoes it, or does nothing at all and lets the veto window run out — and can stop everything in one action if they change their mind

Finds the page live the next morning on their own domain, or waiting as a draft in their own WordPress — or, where a check still stood against it, finds it unpublished and still theirs to fix, with what held it named
Checks a day later that the page is genuinely reachable, indexable and readable by AI assistants, and sees plainly when one of those checks failed

On the rare occasion the pages worth writing are running short, is told so while the calendar is still full — and, on a day that does carry none, reads which kind of empty day it is: nothing in their market was worth publishing, a page was planned and did not go live, or there is an instruction for them to carry out first
Takes the whole library with them whenever they want — copying one page, exporting everything, or unpublishing a page they regret

JN-004.title: Changing your account, and leaving
JN-004.persona: A paying customer, weeks into the daily loop, who needs to change one thing about their account — or has decided to go

steps.step: Opens Settings to change one thing, and sees the whole of what is theirs to change
Corrects the domain they are measured under, the market they are measured in, and the rivals they are measured against
Changes how and when pages go out, and reconnects a destination that stopped working
Turns off an email they no longer want
Updates the card, checks an invoice, or cancels the plan
Moves the address they sign in with, or signs out
Takes everything they have published away with them
Pulls their pages off the web, or closes the account for good
Comes back after the plan has lapsed, signs in with a fresh link, and takes their pages or resumes — having been told twice beforehand which day the pages ReachKit hosts for them stop being served

JN-005.title: The Monday check-in — is any of this actually working?
JN-005.persona: paying solo founder, weeks into the subscription, judging whether to keep paying

steps.step: Opens Monday's email and reads what moved this week, with sections simply absent where nothing could be measured — and, on a week only partly measured, one line naming which sections could not be

Opens the app to Overview and reads whether they appear in more searches than they did, with every number carrying its change or its goal — or, on a week the product could not measure, reads that instead of a number
Reads how far ahead each competitor they confirmed still is — as a ratio, or as plain numbers while they appear in fewer than ten searches — and whether that distance is shrinking

Reads the verdict on each page they published — working, too early to judge, not working, or no longer judgeable because the test it was given stopped being measurable — against the test that page was created with, and on a week only partly measured reads instead, for each page the week could not judge, that it was not measured this week

JN-006.title: The domain owner — correcting or removing a public report about my business
JN-006.persona: the owner of a business whose domain someone else scanned, who has never used ReachKit and did not ask for a report about them to exist

steps.step: Opens a public report about their own domain, sent to them by someone else — never found in a search, because no report is indexed — and reads all of it with no account, session or payment

Reads which market the report measured their business in — shown on every report — and corrects it, the one correction a free report allows to whoever is reading, then reads the report re-measured against the business they actually run
Or, wanting the report gone rather than corrected, reads on the report itself the address to write to and asks there for it to be removed
Returns within five working days and finds the address no longer serving the report, and one written line there naming the address that would bring it back

REQ-047.title: Every page proposed comes from measured evidence, states the test that would prove it worked, and targets only what the customer could win

rests-on.claim: A top-10 containing a domain that ranks for no more than the greater of 500 searches and five times the customer's own count marks a target a small site can realistically win, and leaves a non-empty winnable set for a customer at zero.

A domain ranking for no more than the greater of 100 searches and twice the customer's own count reads to the customer as a site roughly their own size, which is what the word Winnable promises them. The floor is 100 rather than 500 because at 500 this expression and criterion 9's are equal for every customer ranking below 250 searches, so every queued target banded Winnable and the Reach band was unreachable for the cold-start founder.

REQ-075.title: The customer chooses which recurring emails they receive

rests-on.claim: The three toggles in BUILD §4.7 are the three recurring emails a paying customer receives — draft-ready, published, weekly — and every other kind in the set REQ-064 registers is transactional or pre-purchase and therefore not togglable. What a toggle reaches is an occasion rather than a whole kind: one occasion of a togglable kind is itself transactional and stays outside these toggles — the draft-ready mail sent under autopilot at a veto window of zero, which is the whole of the customer's telling that a page is going live and which REQ-057 criterion 7 keeps unsuppressible.

REQ-076.title: Billing and cancellation are self-service, and cancelling keeps everything running to the paid-through date

rests-on.claim: Stripe's customer portal can be configured so that a customer adds or corrects the tax ID (VAT number) on their own billing record there. Nothing in this corpus establishes that capability: BUILD.md §13 names the portal only for card and cancellation, and puts the VAT ID field at Checkout. Criterion 2 rests on it (rule 1.2 — the vendor behaviour is asserted from outside the corpus and is unverified in it).

Every customer-facing date this requirement states — the next invoice date, the paid-through date access ends on — is stated in the customer's own stated time zone, the single stored preference REQ-073 criterion 3 governs.

REQ-095.title: Supply runs a month deep, is topped up every week, and a customer whose supply is short is told when we know it — not when the calendar empties

rests-on.claim: The onboarding deep pass, on the pinned battery (12 question SERPs, up to 13 target SERPs, rival ranked rows, two suggestion calls, up to 25 measured pages), can yield 30 qualifying unused opportunities for a customer who ranks for nothing — the default customer under the cold-start law. No yield has been measured; `BUILD.md` §16 milestone 6 ('Real supply fills the calendar; empty days honest') is the first point at which it can be.

Seven unused opportunities — one week of pages — is the count at which a customer must be told supply is short, because the weekly re-measurement (REQ-065 criterion 1) is the only event that replenishes supply and cannot arrive sooner than the following Monday.
